title: Revision 3: Regional innovation systems and industrial restructuring

chapters.title: The theme in one minute
chapters.readings: Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 16; Fløysand & Jakobsen 2016, p. 324
paragraphs: In plain words, a regional innovation system is the way one region learns. It is the firms, the knowledge organisations and the public agencies that work together inside a region, and the rules that hold them together.

Fløysand and colleagues, 2022, take their definition from Cooke. A regional innovation system is a set of interacting subsystems of knowledge infrastructure and commercial exploitation. The subsystems are knowledge, industry and governance, and they are linked to the wider world.

Why does the course spend a theme on this? Because restructuring happens in regions. A country can grow and a region inside it can stagnate, or the other way round. The regional level is where you can see related industries, clusters and political choices meet.

The Norwegian case is Western Norway. Two neighbouring regions, Hordaland and Rogaland, both depend on petroleum, and they responded differently to the green shift. That difference is the heart of this theme.
Remember: a region's knowledge, industry and rules, and two Norwegian regions that went different ways.

checks.q: What is a regional innovation system?
checks.a: A set of interacting subsystems of knowledge infrastructure and commercial exploitation.

checks.q: Which two regions does the theme compare?

chapters.title: The key ideas
chapters.readings: Fløysand & Jakobsen 2016, pp. 328, 330; Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 15
paragraphs: Four ideas carry the theme.

The first is related variety. Fløysand and Jakobsen, 2016, describe industries that differ but are related, which gives a region room to combine them. A region with related variety can renew without starting from nothing.

The second is the four trajectories. A path can be exhausted, extended, renewed or created. Extension means more of the same. Creation means a new industry. The two middle cases are where most policy lives.

The third is institutional work. Fløysand and colleagues, 2022, following Lawrence and colleagues, describe it as the work actors do to affect institutions. Actors can maintain, create, change or disrupt the rules.

The fourth is the difference between a diversified and a specialized system. A diversified region has many related sectors and many networks. A specialized region has one dominant industry and a tighter set of leaders.
Put them together and you have the argument of the theme. Related variety and open institutions help a region restructure. Specialisation and closed institutions can hold it in place.

There is a fifth idea that ties the theme to policy. A cluster programme can recognize an industry and still freeze it. Fløysand and Jakobsen, 2016, make this point about specialisation. Being admitted to a national programme confirms that an industry has potential, but it can also reward continuity. A region that celebrates its mature cluster may find it harder to fund the experiments that would create the next one. That is why the theme keeps both levels in view, the cluster and the experiment.
Remember: related variety, four trajectories, institutional work and the difference between diversified and specialized systems.

checks.a: Industries that differ but are related, which gives a region room to combine them.

checks.q: What are the four trajectories of a path?

chapters.title: The model, step by step
paragraphs: The first model is simple. Regional renewal has three levels.
First, the industry level, where cluster dynamics decide whether firms cooperate or compete.
Second, the firm level, where related variety decides what a firm can borrow from its neighbours.
Third, the individual level, where entrepreneurship decides who starts something new.

The second model is the four trajectories. First, path exhaustion, when an industry weakens and loses its base. Second, path extension, when a region does more of the same. Third, path renewal, when it upgrades the industry with new products. Fourth, path creation, when it develops a new industry rather than extending an old one.
The two models fit together. The three levels explain what renewal is made of, and the four trajectories explain what it looks like when it happens.
Remember: three levels of renewal, and four trajectories that a path can take.

checks.q: What are the three levels of regional renewal?
checks.a: The industry level, the firm level and the individual level.
Developing a new industry rather than extending an old one.

chapters.title: Norway examples
chapters.readings: Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 15; Fløysand & Jakobsen 2016, p. 337
paragraphs: Hordaland and Rogaland are the two examples you need.
In Hordaland, Fløysand and colleagues, 2022, find a diversified and interactive system. Collective work across clusters legitimized a green shift. The region could combine what it had.
In Rogaland, the same study finds a specialized and tightly led system. Individual work delegitimized the green shift, and the petroleum path held.

There is also a smaller example. Fløysand and Jakobsen, 2016, describe a pilot for microalgae at Mongstad, which would join oil knowledge to marine knowledge in fish feed. That is related variety at work, if it succeeds.
Notice what the cases do not say. They do not say that one region is better than the other. They say that the same vision can produce different outcomes when the system around it is different.
Remember: Hordaland diversified and open, Rogaland specialized and tight, and Mongstad as a small case of related variety.

checks.q: What did collective work do in Hordaland?
checks.a: It legitimized a green shift across clusters.

checks.q: What would the Mongstad pilot join?
checks.a: Oil knowledge and marine knowledge, in fish feed.

chapters.title: How the exam asks about it
chapters.readings: Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 15; Fløysand & Jakobsen 2016, p. 330
paragraphs: Two questions fit this theme.

The first is the discussion question of June 2025. It asks in what way a regional innovation system can promote or inhibit industrial restructuring. The wording invites both sides, and the two Norwegian regions give you both.

The second is the concept question of the same paper, which asks what you understand by a regional innovation system, institutional work and sustainability. This theme gives you the first two terms, and the sustainability theme gives you the third.

Here is the shape of a good answer. Define the system with Cooke. Add related variety as the resource a region can draw on. Then use the two regions. Say what promoted restructuring in Hordaland and what inhibited it in Rogaland. End by saying that the same vision can fail when the system is tight.

One more move helps. Say clearly that a system can do both at once. It can promote restructuring in one part of the region and slow it in another. Hordaland shows this inside one region, where some clusters moved towards green work while petroleum suppliers kept their old markets. A strong answer names that split rather than choosing one side.
Remember: define the system, add related variety, and show both sides with the two regions.

checks.q: Which question asks you to show both sides?
checks.a: The question on how a regional system can promote or inhibit restructuring.

checks.q: Which term does this theme not define for the June concept question?
checks.a: Sustainability, which the sustainability theme supplies.

chapters.title: Test yourself
chapters.readings: Fløysand & Jakobsen 2016, pp. 324, 330; Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 15
paragraphs: Question one. What makes a region able to renew without starting from nothing?
Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. Related variety. When a region has industries that differ but are related, firms can combine what they already know into something new.
Question two. Why did Hordaland and Rogaland respond differently to the same green vision?
Pause the audio and answer in your head.

Here is the answer. Because their systems differed. Hordaland had a diversified and interactive system, where collective work legitimized the shift. Rogaland had a specialized and tightly led system, where individual work legitimized the petroleum path instead.
Question three. What is the difference between path extension and path creation?
Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. Extension is more of the same, an existing industry continuing. Creation is a new industry, developed rather than extended from an old one.
Remember: related variety gives a region options, and its system decides whether it uses them.

checks.q: What is the difference between a diversified and a specialized region?
checks.a: A diversified region has many related sectors and networks, a specialized one has a dominant industry and tight leadership.

checks.q: What can a cluster programme do to a specialized region?
checks.a: It can reward continuity, which makes experiments harder to fund.
